51	        {
52	          $comment:
53	            'Transitional basis-pinning rule, scoped ENTIRELY to the observation form. basisRevision is declared without constraints at generated level, because a legacy artifact may already carry that key with any value — including a symbolic ref such as "HEAD" — and constraining it globally would invalidate a document that was valid before this amendment. The requirement AND the object-ID pattern therefore live only in this then branch, which applies only once an observation-form entry is present. An EMPTY coChange array triggers nothing: schema validation cannot tell an empty array written by a legacy producer from one written by an observation producer, so an unpinned empty array is defined as legacy/unknown rather than as evidence of zero. New producers carry the stronger obligation, stated in the producer profile.',
54	          if: {
55	            required: ['coChange'],
56	            properties: { coChange: { contains: { required: ['support'] } } },
57	          },
58	          then: {
59	            required: ['basisRevision'],
60	            properties: {
61	              basisRevision: {
62	                type: 'string',
63	                pattern: '^([0-9a-f]{40}|[0-9a-f]{64})$',
64	              },
65	            },
66	          },
67	        },
68	      ],
69	      properties: {
70	        specVersion: { enum: ['0.3', '0.4'] as const },
71	        generatedAt: { type: 'string', format: 'date-time' },
72	        basisRevision: {
73	          description:
74	            'The repository revision the observations in this section were computed from. UNCONSTRAINED HERE, deliberately: a legacy artifact may already carry this key with any value, including a symbolic ref such as "HEAD", and constraining it globally would invalidate a document that was valid before the observation form existed. The contract is imposed by the conditional rule on this object, and applies only where an observation-form coChange entry is present. Under that rule the value is the full-length lowercase hexadecimal Git object name of the commit at the tip of the analyzed history — 40 characters for SHA-1, 64 for SHA-256 — because a pin that does not name exactly one commit permanently cannot be recounted against; abbreviated object names, branch names and tags are rejected there. Declared once here; never repeated per observation. A producer emitting the observation form must declare a conforming value whenever generated.coChange exists at all, including when the array is empty; that stronger obligation belongs to the producer profile, because an empty array carries nothing for schema validation to discriminate on.',

81	            version: { type: 'string' },
82	          },

87	          items: {

93	            },

97	          type: 'object',
98	          description:

111	          description:
112	            'Machine-derived co-change pairs. An entry carrying both is invalid — the two are different contracts, and a reader cannot know which was measured. An entry carrying neither is invalid. The array is also HOMOGENEOUS: every entry is in the legacy form, or every entry is in the observation form. A mixed array is invalid, because one artifact would then carry two different meanings of occurrences with nothing at the collection level saying so, and a reader aggregating across entries would silently combine them. An empty array satisfies both branches and asserts nothing about which form its producer would have used. New producers emit only the observation form; legacy acceptance exists so that already-published artifacts keep validating, and is removed at the next document-profile change. A qualifying commit is one inside the analysis boundary declared by the producer — the same boundary that governs every other observation in this section, and reachable from generated.basisRevision. This schema does not define that boundary: history window, merge handling, rename following and path normalization are producer-profile concerns. It requires only that one boundary is applied identically to support and occurrences in every entry. The generated flag is a CLASSIFICATION, not an observation, and it is optional in the observation form: an entry that omits it makes no claim either way, and a reader must not read absence as false. See the flag\'s own description for the three-state reading.',

The explicit not clauses make each branch reject the other representation on its own, independently of how many branches happen to match.",
122	            oneOf: [
123	              {
124	                title: 'legacy form',
125	                required: ['rate', 'generated'] as const,
126	                not: { required: ['support'] as const },
127	              },
128	              {
129	                title: 'observation form',
130	                required: ['support'] as const,
131	                not: { required: ['rate'] as const },
132	                properties: { occurrences: { minimum: 1 } },
133	              },
134	            ],
135	            properties: {

137	                type: 'array',
138	                items: { type: 'string' },
139	                minItems: 2,
140	                maxItems: 2,
141	                description:
142	                  'Unordered pair (set semantics — position is NOT meaningful; join by membership, not index). Each entry is a repository-root-relative POSIX path.',
143	              },
144	              rate: {
145	                type: 'number',
146	                minimum: 0,
147	                maximum: 1,
148	                description:
149	                  'LEGACY FORM ONLY, and deprecated. A derived value the standard no longer stores: it is continuous, so every new commit moves it, and it forces one analytical reading on every consumer. Retained solely so artifacts published before the observation form keep validating at generated.specVersion 0.4. New producers must not emit it, and must not emit it alongside support. Removed at the next document-profile change.',
150	              },
151	              support: {
152	                type: 'integer',
153	                minimum: 0,
154	                description:
155	                  'OBSERVATION FORM. The number of distinct qualifying commits in which BOTH files changed. Commits are counted, not file events or ordered relationships: a commit that touches either file more than once counts once. Symmetric — swapping the two entries of files does not change it. Never exceeds occurrences, since the commits it counts are a subset of those occurrences counts.',
156	              },
157	              occurrences: {
158	                type: 'integer',
159	                minimum: 0,
160	                description:
161	                  'The denominator, present in both forms — but its referent is determined by the form, so a reader must establish the form before reading it. In the OBSERVATION form (alongside support) it is the number of distinct qualifying commits in which AT LEAST ONE of the two files changed: the symmetric union denominator, counting commits rather than file events, unchanged by swapping the two entries of files. There it is constrained to a MINIMUM OF 1, so support / occurrences is always defined and no reader can produce 0/0, NaN or infinity from a conforming artifact: a pair whose union of qualifying commits is empty was never observed changing at all, so no entry may be emitted for it. Absence of an entry, not a zero denominator, is how an unobserved pair is represented. The standard stores no derived rate, probability, lift or ranking. In the LEGACY form (alongside rate) it carries the pre-amendment meaning, which was never specified normatively, must not be assumed symmetric, and keeps its original minimum of 0 so that published artifacts stay valid. Values must not be compared across the two forms.',
162	              },
163	              generated: {
164	                type: 'boolean',
165	                description:
166	                  'OPTIONAL IN THE OBSERVATION FORM, REQUIRED IN THE LEGACY FORM. A classification, not an observation: true asserts the pair is tooling-coupled (a lockfile and its manifest, a generated file and its source) and that a consumer surfacing real source couplings should skip it. Unlike support and occurrences, it cannot be read off the commit graph — it requires a judgement about what a file IS, and no portable deterministic classifier from public repository inputs is specified by this standard. It is therefore THREE-STATE for readers: true means classified tooling-coupled; false means classified NOT tooling-coupled; ABSENT means the producer performed no classification and asserts nothing. A reader must not collapse absent into false — that would convert a producer\'s silence into a positive claim that the pair is a real source coupling, which is exactly the unsupported certainty this form declines to require. A new producer omits the flag unless it implements a public, deterministic, perturbation-tested classifier, and two producers that classify the same pair differently are both conformant, so the flag is not a comparison surface between producers. findings.summary: The new `provenance` property is added only to the TypeScript-authored schema.ts mirror, not to the published packages/spec/schema/v1.json artifact, breaking the repo's split-brain guard.
findings.failure_scenario: packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:324-329 ('workspaceJsonSchema top-level property keys match schema/v1.json') sorts and compares Object.keys(workspaceJsonSchema.properties) against Object.keys(JSON.parse(schema/v1.json).properties). After this diff, schema.ts's key list includes 'provenance' while schema/v1.json (confirmed via grep — no 'provenance' key present) does not, so the two arrays differ and this test fails. The two schema mirrors are the published contract independent implementers build from (per the file's own test comments at index.test.ts:314-315), so shipping this change leaves the published JSON schema silently missing the new field while the TS source has it.

findings.summary: provenance.basisRevision duplicates generated.basisRevision's name/purpose but with none of its validation contract, creating two differently-constrained fields with the same meaning.
findings.failure_scenario: generated.basisRevision (schema.ts:72-75, with the conditional rule at schema.ts:50-67) is required, when coChange uses the observation form, to be a full 40- or 64-character lowercase hex Git object id — explicitly rejecting symbolic refs like 'HEAD', 'main', or 'refs/heads/main' (enforced by packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:1444-1446). The new top-level provenance.basisRevision (schema.ts:231-234) is a bare `{ type: 'string' }` with no pattern and no relation to coChange, so a producer can legally set provenance.basisRevision to 'HEAD' or any arbitrary string. A consumer that doesn't know to distinguish the two fields by their container can easily read the unconstrained provenance.basisRevision believing it carries the same 'names exactly one commit, can be recounted against' guarantee that generated.basisRevision was specifically designed (per its extensive schema.ts:74 description) to provide, and get a mutable ref instead of a pinned commit.

findings.summary: The TypeScript document types (WorkspaceJsonV3/WorkspaceJsonV4) were not updated with a `provenance` field and have no top-level index signature, so the new schema-level field has no corresponding, type-checked representation in the SDK's own type surface.
findings.failure_scenario: WorkspaceJsonV4 (types.ts:245-279) lists version/manual/generated/agents/health only, with no `[key: string]: unknown` at the top level (unlike its nested `manual`/`generated`/`health` sub-objects, which do have index signatures at types.ts:80, :90, :99). Code constructing a WorkspaceJsonV4 object literal with a `provenance` field would fail TS excess-property checking, and code reading `doc.provenance` off a validated document gets no type support — the schema now accepts a field the SDK's own types don't know exists, another symptom of the same split-brain as the v1.json mismatch above.

content.text:
## Summary

The diff adds a `provenance` object to `workspaceJsonSchema` in `packages/spec/src/schema.ts` but introduces three correctness problems:

1. **Split-brain with the published schema artifact** (`packages/spec/src/schema.ts:228` vs `packages/spec/schema/v1.json`): the repo maintains two mirrors of the schema and has an explicit test (`packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:324-329`) asserting their top-level property keys match. `schema/v1.json` has no `provenance` key, so this test will fail — the diff only touched one mirror.

2. **Duplicate, inconsistently-constrained `basisRevision`** (`schema.ts:231-234` vs the existing `generated.basisRevision` at `schema.ts:72-75`): the existing field has a carefully designed, heavily-documented and tested contract requiring a full 40/64-char hex commit SHA (rejecting `HEAD`, branch names, etc. — see `index.test.ts:1444-1446`). The new `provenance.basisRevision` is an unconstrained plain string with the same name and stated purpose ("the revision it was generated from"), so producers/consumers now have two same-named, differently-guaranteed fields for the same concept.

3. **TypeScript types not updated** (`packages/spec/src/types.ts:245-279`): `WorkspaceJsonV3`/`WorkspaceJsonV4` have no `provenance` field and, unlike their nested sub-objects, no top-level index signature — so the schema now accepts data the SDK's own types can't represent.

FILES INSPECTED
- packages/spec/src/schema.ts
- packages/spec/src/types.ts
- packages/spec/src/index.test.ts
- packages/spec/schema/v1.json

1. **Split-brain with the published schema artifact** (`packages/spec/src/schema.ts:228` vs `packages/spec/schema/v1.json`): the repo maintains two mirrors of the schema and has an explicit test (`packages/spec/src/index.test.ts:324-329`) asserting their top-level property keys match. `schema/v1.json` has no `provenance` key, so this test will fail — the diff only touched one mirror.

2. **Duplicate, inconsistently-constrained `basisRevision`** (`schema.ts:231-234` vs the existing `generated.basisRevision` at `schema.ts:72-75`): the existing field has a carefully designed, heavily-documented and tested contract requiring a full 40/64-char hex commit SHA (rejecting `HEAD`, branch names, etc. — see `index.test.ts:1444-1446`). The new `provenance.basisRevision` is an unconstrained plain string with the same name and stated purpose ("the revision it was generated from"), so producers/consumers now have two same-named, differently-guaranteed fields for the same concept.

3. **TypeScript types not updated** (`packages/spec/src/types.ts:245-279`): `WorkspaceJsonV3`/`WorkspaceJsonV4` have no `provenance` field and, unlike their nested sub-objects, no top-level index signature — so the schema now accepts data the SDK's own types can't represent.
